note: The two sets are nearly identical, sharing 23 of 25 claims verbatim and the same omissions. The only real differences are in the two claims about wiring 150: Set A uses the vague attributes 'material' and 'conductor', while Set B binds the same values to the more precise properties 'conductor material' and 'conductor configuration'. Set B's minor blemish is naming the same entity both 'Wiring 150/151' and 'Wiring Symbol 150/151'. Both sets correctly read the schedule rows and neither invents values.
remarks: Both sets omit several schedule facts: 150's #4G. ground and 2-1/2"C. conduit, 20's #12G. ground, 33's 6#10 conductors, 50's 3#6 conductors, and 10's #12/2WG. cable. The 'conditions: C.' field on conduit claims is a fragment of the quote ('1"C.'), not a real operating condition. Set B states the same entities under two names ('Wiring 150'/'Wiring Symbol 150', 'Wiring 151'/'Wiring Symbol 151'), which is a consistency problem even though the facts are distinct. The text layer is jumbled (row labels detached from descriptions, e.g. '1, 3W.' garbled), so row-to-value binding had to be checked against the image; both sets did this correctly.
